To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel avionics partition architecture that is successfully implemented and certifiable as a part of a helicopter avionics.

the developed partitioning system is: - A system that can be used to partition software components of different criticality levels into one single system, - A system that has been successfully implemented and certified, and - A system that is based on the use of two processor features: a MMU and a processor with protection levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a partitioning architecture which supports the development of airborne systems with a high degree of software complexity.
the design of a partitioning architecture that can be used for the development of avionics software.
the development and certification of partitioning architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the partitioning architecture as developed and implemented is a mature, reliable and cost-effective solution to support the development of software for airborne systems.
the implemented partitioning architecture is very suitable for safety critical avionics software.
the implemented partitioning architecture is an excellent solution for the partitioning problem of the avionic software in the helicopter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed partitioning solution has proven to be very successful and has a high degree of reusability and portability.
partitioning is a viable and cost-effective solution for safety-critical software.

we developed a partitioning architecture that is successfully certified for use in safety critical airborne systems, that is applicable to other hardware, that can be extended to other applications, that is easy to port and that induces only a small resource overhead.
The main takeaway from our work is that

partitioning is a viable solution for reducing the cost of software development of airborne systems without compromising the functionality of the safety-critical components and thus the certification of the airborne system.
partitioning can be successfully applied in practice and that the benefits outweigh the costs.
it is feasible to partition safety-critical airborne software in practice.
